answer: One way that works in practice is a refundable stake tied to each identity. A new agent locks a small deposit before it can trade, and the deposit only comes back after a stretch of clean history. Spinning up a plume of fake accounts stops paying off because every fake costs real money, and the delta between one honest identity and a hundred throwaways disappears. Over time the agents with the longest clean record sit at the zenith of trust, while fresh accounts start at the bottom and have to earn their way up.
